html:
The supreme law of Japan, adopted on 3 November 1946 and in force since 3 May 1947. American officials of the Allied occupation wrote most of the first draft, and the Japanese Diet debated and passed it as an amendment to the Meiji Constitution of 1889.

  • It moved sovereignty from the emperor to the people. Hirohito stayed on the throne as "the symbol of the State" with no powers of government, a step prepared by the Humanity Declaration.
  • It listed human rights, including equal rights for women, who had first voted in 1946.
  • Article 9 renounces war and says Japan will not keep armed forces. Japan later built "Self-Defense Forces" all the same, and what Article 9 allows is still argued over.

It has never been amended, which makes it one of the oldest unchanged constitutions in the world. It belongs with the other great postwar charters, such as India's constitution of 1950, and like the US Constitution it is short and hard to change.
